This Deva is the person of vaṭajjhāsaya, vaṭṭābhirata like Anāthapindika and Visākhā. He will attain final Parinibbāna in Akaniṭṭha abode after living in pleasure in six celestial abodes in order.
pn:
Anekavaṇṇa. A Devaputta in Tāvatiṁsa, who, because of his good deeds, excelled even Sakka in majesty. When he appeared in the streets of Tāvatiṁsa, Sakka fled in shame (Dhp-a.i.426-7).

The Vimānavatthu (pp.74-5; Vv-a.318ff) gives his past story which he revealed to Moggallāna. He had been a monk under Sumedha Buddha, but later, feeling disheartened, left the Saṅgha. When the Buddha died he was seized with repentance for having lost his opportunity, and paid homage to the Buddha’s shrine and observed the precepts.
